meaning.evidence: Every duty, condition and qualification kept accurately, including the Selective Service line, PIV, the 18-semester-hour note and the AFGE unit: "Only postgrad study beyond the first year (18 semester hours) counts for the GS-9."

sense.evidence: Fits: "part-time work gets counted pro rata", "all the program goals get ticked off", "the chance to work from home" for telework.

authenticity.evidence: Natural plain Australian English ("postgrad", "Have a look at"), though "You've gotta" is a little forced in a job ad and "Specialized Experience" keeps US spelling beside "specialised".

register.evidence: More plain-English rewrite than level-3 Aussie: little idiom beyond "ticked off" and "gotta" ("Understand and properly use the technical resources available for, and tied to").

tone.evidence: Still a clear, official job ad, made friendlier.

flow.evidence: Reads easily: "If you get picked at a lower grade level, you'll get the chance to learn how to do all of these duties".

variety.evidence: Little slang to vary; "gotta" twice, "Have a look" twice.

essence.evidence: Plainly the NARA vacancy, structure intact.

problems.quote: You've gotta pass a background check.
problems.original: Must successfully complete a background investigation.
problems.why: "gotta" is a stock casualism, a touch off in an ad.

problems.original: Specialized Experience: For the GS-09, you must have one year of specialized experience

problems.original: Understand and properly use the technical resources available for, and associated with

A.summary: Accurate and readable plain-English version, lighter on Aussie than the brief asks.

meaning.evidence: All requirements kept accurately; additions are colour ("no worries", "Your experience can come from any paddock").

sense.evidence: Exact: "learn the whole box and dice", "running the show" for leading others, "new starter", "right to work", "tick these boxes", "on your CV".

authenticity.evidence: Sounds like an Australian HR officer talking: "Get your head around what the customers need", "Know your way around the technical gear".

register.evidence: Level 3: idiom throughout without losing the ad's function; no swearing.

tone.evidence: Still an official vacancy notice, warmer in voice.

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly: "Keep the work on track, whether you're going it alone, pulling your weight in a team or running the show".

problems.quote: Your experience can come from any paddock
problems.original: The experience may have been gained in either the public, private sector or volunteer service
problems.why: "paddock" is a slightly forced image here.

B.summary: A natural, accurate and fully level-3 retelling of the ad.

meaning.evidence: "Must be U.S. Battlers or U.S. Nationals" turns the citizenship requirement into nonsense; the rest is the original verbatim.

sense.evidence: "Battlers" for Citizens, "the paddock(s) covered by the position" for field(s): wrong senses.

authenticity.evidence: Bolt-ons on untouched text: "Bugger me, go through a Personal Identity Verification", "Bloody hell, specialised experience".

register.evidence: Essentially untranslated ("The following are the duties of this position at the GS-12"); far under level 3.

tone.evidence: An official ad with random oaths, which jar badly.

flow.evidence: Readable because it is the original, but the inserted oaths break sentences.

variety.evidence: Two oaths and two swaps; nothing to vary.

essence.evidence: Recognisably the ad, but with its key eligibility line garbled.
